source_text:
ἔστιν ὡς σῶμα ἡνωμένον κεφαλῇ, καὶ πανταχοῦ κεφαλὴν τῆς ἐκκλησίας τὸν
Χριστὸν λέγει. καὶ ἐστὲ ἐν αὐτῷ πεπληρωμένοι, ἀντὶ τοῦ δι' αὐτοῦ πεπληρωμένοι.
πεπληρωμένοι δὲ τίνος; δηλονότι τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος. ὅς ἐστι κεφαλὴ πάσης ἀρχῆς
καὶ ἐξουσίας. οὐ μόνον, φησί, τῆς ἐκκλησίας ἐστὶ κεφαλή–τοῦτο γὰρ τῆς οἰκονομίας
ἴδιον–ἀλλὰ καὶ πάσης ἀοράτου δυνάμεως, ἐπεὶ καὶ δημιουργὸς αὐτῆς ἐστιν. Τὴν
ἐκκλησίαν λέγει πεπληρωμένην ὑπὸ τῆς θεότητος αὐτοῦ, καθὼς ἀλλαχοῦ φησιν· τοῦ
τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσι πληρουμένου. τὸ δὲ σωματικῶς ἐνταῦθα ὡς ἐν κεφαλῇ σῶμα. πῶς
οὖν οὐκ ἐπήγαγεν· ἥτις ἐστὶν ἡ ἐκκλησία; Kol 2,11 Τοῦτ' ἔστι περιτεμὼν ἡμᾶς ἐκ τῆς
ἁμαρτίας τῆς σαρκὸς διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος ἐζωοποίησεν ἑαυτῷ. ὥστε τὸ ἐν Χριστῷ
βάπτισμα περιτομὴ πνευματική· περικόπτει γὰρ τῶν πιστευόντων τὰς ἁμαρτίας. Kol
2,12–13 ∆ιὰ γὰρ τοῦ βαπτίσματος ἡ περιαίρεσις καὶ ἡ περιτομὴ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν.
συνταφέντες αὐτῷ ἐν τῷ βαπτίσματι, ἐν ᾧ καὶ συνηγέρθητε. οἱ βαπτιζόμενοι ἐν τῷ
αἵματι τοῦ Χριστοῦ κοινωνεῖν αὐτῷ τοῦ θανάτου ὁμολογοῦσι διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος·
κοινωνήσαντες δὲ αὐτῷ τοῦ θανάτου, ἀKolούθως καὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως
ἀπολαύσουσιν. ἔστι δὲ διπλοῦς ὁ τῆς ἀναστάσεως λόγος· ὁ μὲν γὰρ εἷς πνευματικός,
ὁ δὲ ἕτερος σωματικός. ἀναστήσεται μὲν γὰρ πᾶσα σὰρξ ἀνθρώπων διὰ τὴν Χριστοῦ
ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀνάστασιν, ἀλλ' ὅσοι μὲν οὐκ ἐβαπτίσθησαν ἐν Χριστῷ, ἀλλ' ἐναπέθανον
αὐτῶν τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ, οὗτοι τῆς μὲν κοινῆς ἀναστάσεως μεθέξουσιν, τῆς δὲ
ἀπολυτρώσεως καὶ τῆς ἐπαγγελίας οὐκ 323 ἀπολαύσουσιν. ὅσοι δὲ εἰς Χριστὸν
ἐβαπτίσθησαν, οὗτοι καὶ πρὸ τῆς κοινῆς ἀναστάσεως ἑτέρας ἀναστάσεως δωρεὰν
ἐκέρδαναν· ἤδη γὰρ ἀπὸ τοῦ θανάτου τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἐξανέστησαν. διὸ καὶ εἶπεν· ἐν
ᾧ καὶ συνηγέρθητε, οὐκ «ἐν ᾧ συνεγερθήσεσθε». οἱ οὖν ἐγερθέντες ἀπὸ τοῦ θανάτου
τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν πῶς ἔτι πολιτεύσονται ὡς πάλιν ἀποθανούμενοι; οὐκοῦν μάτην
ἀνέστησαν; εἰ δὲ ὡς ἀεὶ ζήσοντες, οὐκ ἄρα κατὰ σάρκα διαζῶσι ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις τῆς
σαρκὸς δουλεύοντες, ἀλλὰ κατὰ πνεῦμα πολιτεύσονται. σῶμα ἁμαρτίας καλεῖ τὰς
πράξεις τὰς ἀτόπους· αὗται γὰρ διὰ σώματος τελοῦνται. περιτομὴ οὖν Χριστοῦ τὸ
βάπτισμα· περιαιρεῖ γὰρ τὸ σῶμα τῆς ἁμαρτίας τὴν ἀκροβυστίαν. ὡς περιττὸν δὲ
ἀκροβυστία Ἰουδαίῳ, οὕτως ἁμαρτία ψυχῇ καὶ σώματι. διόλου δὲ τῇ τροπῇ
παρέμεινεν. ἀκροβυστίαν δὲ σαρκὸς τὴν ἁμαρτίαν λέγει. Kol 2,14–15 Ὅτε ἐδόθη ὁ
νόμος ὁ καταρώμενος τοὺς παραβαίνοντας, πᾶς ὁ λαὸς Ἰσραὴλ ἑστὼς ἐβόα, καὶ
συγκατετίθετο τοῖς λεγομένοις καταδεχόμενος αὐτά, καὶ ἡ συγκατάθεσις ὥσπερ
χειρόγραφον γέγονεν. τοῦτο οὖν τὸ χειρόγραφον, τὴν συγκατάθεσιν τὴν πρὸς τὸν
νόμον, ἐξήλειψε τοῖς ἑαυτοῦ δόγμασιν ὁ Χριστός· ἐδογμάτισε γὰρ κατὰ τῶν
ἐπιτηρήσεων τοῦ νόμου, ὡς ἐπὶ τῶν βρωμάτων ὅτι οὐ τὰ εἰσερχόμενα ἀλλὰ τὰ
ἐξερχόμενα κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς τηρήσεως τοῦ σαββάτου, ὅτι ἐν τῷ
σαββάτῳ ἐθεράπευσεν· καὶ ἕτερα τοιαῦτα πολλά τις ἐπιτηρήσας εὑρήσει.
προηγουμένως οὖν τοῦ νόμου τὰς τιμωρίας τὰς κατὰ τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν τοῖς δόγμασι
τῆς ἁμαρτίας κατήργησεν, δοὺς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν καὶ μετάνοιαν εἰς σωτηρίαν.
ἐπειδὴ δὲ ἐν ταῖς κατάραις ὁ λαὸς ἔλεγε τὸ ἀμήν, ὥσπερ ὑπόγραφον χειρόγραφον
ἐβλήθη. Ἀπεκδυσάμενος τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ τὰς ἐξουσίας ἐδειγμάτισεν ἐν παρρησίᾳ, 324
θριαμβεύσας ἐν τῷ σταυρῷ. ἐπειδὴ διὰ τῆς ἀπεκδύσεως καὶ τῆς ἀποθέσεως τῆς
σαρκὸς τὰς ἐναντίας δυνάμεις καθεῖλεν, ἀπεκδυσάμενος τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ τὰς ἐξουσίας
ἐδειγμάτισεν ἐν παρρησίᾳ, θριαμβεύσας αὐτοὺς ἐν αὐτῷ. μέχρι γὰρ τοῦ σταυροῦ καὶ
αὐτοῦ τοῦ θανάτου ἐλάνθανεν ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν ὅτι καὶ θεὸς ἦν καὶ θεοῦ υἱός, καὶ ταῖς
μὲν θαυματουργίαις ἔπληττεν, τῷ δὲ σώματι ἐκαλύπτετο· διὸ καὶ ἐπείρασεν αὐτὸν ὁ
σατανᾶς, βουλόμενος μαθεῖν εἰ αὐτός ἐστιν ὁ ὑπὸ τῶν προφητῶν κηρυττόμενος, ἵνα
εἰ μάθῃ ὅτι αὐτός ἐστιν, ἐμποδίσῃ τὴν οἰκονομίαν. ἀλλ' οὐδὲν ἤνυεν ὁ πονηρός, οὐδὲ
γὰρ ἠδυνήθη μαθεῖν· τέως οὖν ἐλάνθανεν ὁ Χριστός. ἐπειδὴ δὲ προσηλώθη καὶ
ἀπέθανε καὶ ἐτάφη καὶ ἀνέστη καὶ πάντα τὰ τῆς οἰκονομίας ἐπλήρωσεν,
ἀπεξεδύσατο μὲν τὸ λανθάνειν, γυμνῇ δὲ τῇ κεφαλῇ ὁρᾶν τὴν θεότητα μετὰ τοῦ
σώματος οὖσαν ἐδείκνυεν. πρῶτον μὲν οὖν ἦν ἔργον θεοῦ ἡ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀνάστασις,
εἶτα ἡ εἰς οὐρανοὺς ἄνοδος, ἔπειτα ἡ διὰ τῶν ὑπηρετῶν καὶ τῶν ἄλλων ἁγίων ἐν τῷ
ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ ἐνέργεια. ἀπεκδυσάμενος οὖν τὸ λανθάνειν ἐν παρρησίᾳ τὰς ἐναντίας
ἐδειγμάτισεν ἐξουσίας. καὶ τίς τούτων ὁ δειγματισμός; ὅτι ἀσθενέστεροι τῶν
pass_a_gloss:
[continuing the Colossians 2:9-10 note] ... is, as a body united to a head; and everywhere he calls Christ head of the church. "And you are filled in him," in place of "filled through him." Filled with what? Clearly with the Holy Spirit. "Who is the head of every rule and authority": not only of the church, he says, is he head, for this is proper to the economy, but also of every invisible power, since he is also its creator.
[Second form, unmarked repetition:] He means the church filled by his godhead, as he says elsewhere: "of him who fills all things in all." And "bodily" here (means) as a body in a head. How then did he not add: "which is the church"?
Colossians 2:11. That is, having circumcised us from the sin of the flesh through baptism he made us alive to himself. So baptism in Christ is a spiritual circumcision; for it cuts away the sins of those who believe.
Colossians 2:12-13. For through baptism (comes) the stripping away and the circumcision of the sins. "Buried with him in baptism, in which you were also raised with him." Those baptized in the blood of Christ confess through baptism that they share with him in death; and having shared with him in death, consequently they will enjoy the resurrection too. And the account of the resurrection is double: the one spiritual, the other bodily. For all flesh of human beings will rise because of Christ's resurrection from the dead; but as many as were not baptized in Christ but died in their unbelief, these will share in the common resurrection but will not enjoy the redemption and the promise. But as many as were baptized into Christ, these even before the common resurrection have gained another resurrection as a gift; for already they have risen up from the death of the sins. Therefore he also said "in which you were also raised with him," not "in which you will be raised with him." So those raised from the death of the sins, how will they still live as people about to die again? Did they then rise in vain? But if (they live) as people who will always live, then they do not live on according to the flesh, slaving to the desires of the flesh, but will live according to the Spirit. He calls the improper deeds the body of sin; for these are carried out through the body. So baptism is Christ's circumcision; for it strips off the body of sin, the foreskin. As the foreskin is superfluous to a Jew, so sin to soul and body. And throughout he kept to the figure. And he calls sin the foreskin of the flesh.
Colossians 2:14-15. When the law that curses those who transgress was given, all the people of Israel, standing, were crying out and assenting to what was said, accepting it; and the assent became like a handwritten bond. This bond, then, the assent toward the law, Christ wiped out by his own decrees; for he decreed against the observances of the law: as concerning foods, that not the things going in but the things going out make a person common (defile); and concerning the keeping of the Sabbath, that he healed on the Sabbath; and anyone who looks will find many other such things. First of all, then, he abolished by his decrees the punishments of the law against sinners for sin, giving forgiveness of sins and repentance for salvation. And since in the curses the people said the Amen, it was set down as a signed bond. "Having stripped off the rulers and the authorities he made a show of them in openness, triumphing in the cross." Since by the stripping off and laying aside of the flesh he brought down the opposing powers, (it says) "having stripped off the rulers and the authorities he made a show of them in openness, triumphing over them in it." For until the cross and death itself our Lord escaped notice as being both God and Son of God; and with his miracles he struck (people) with amazement, but with the body he was covered. Therefore also Satan tempted him, wishing to learn if he is the one proclaimed by the prophets, so that if he learned that he is, he might hinder the economy. But the evil one achieved nothing, for he was not able to learn; so for the time being Christ escaped notice. But when he was nailed and died and was buried and rose and fulfilled all the things of the economy, he stripped off the escaping of notice, and with bare head he showed the godhead to be seen, being with the body. First, then, the work of God was the resurrection from the dead, then the ascent into the heavens, then the working through the servants and the other saints in his name. So having stripped off the escaping of notice, he made a show of the opposing authorities in openness. And what is the show (made) of these? That they have become weaker than [continues in the next section: human beings]
pass_b_english: … is, as a body united to its head; and everywhere he calls Christ the head of the church. “And you are filled in him” stands for “filled through him”. Filled with what? Clearly, with the Holy Spirit. “Who is the head of every rule and authority”: he is head not only of the church, he says, for that belongs to his saving dispensation, but also of every invisible power, since he is its maker as well.
The second catena form adds: … as he says elsewhere, “of him who fills all in all” (Ephesians 1:23). … Why, then, did he not add “which is the church”?

On Colossians 2:11: That is, he circumcised us from the sin of the flesh and made us alive to himself through baptism. So baptism in Christ is a spiritual circumcision, because it cuts away the sins of those who believe.

On Colossians 2:12–13: Through baptism our sins are stripped away and circumcised. “Buried with him in baptism, in which you were also raised with him.” Those baptized in the blood of Christ confess through baptism that they share in his death, and since they have shared in his death, they will also enjoy his resurrection. Resurrection is spoken of in two ways: one spiritual, the other bodily. All human flesh will rise because Christ rose from the dead. But those who were not baptized in Christ and died in their unbelief will share in the common resurrection without enjoying the redemption and the promise. Those who were baptized into Christ, however, have been given another resurrection even before the common one, for they have already risen from the death of their sins. That is why he said, “in which you were also raised with him”, not “in which you will be raised with him”. Those, then, who have been raised from the death of their sins: how can they still live as people who are going to die again? Did they rise for nothing? If they live as people who will live for ever, they no longer spend their lives according to the flesh as slaves to its desires; they will live according to the Spirit. He calls wrong deeds “the body of sin”, because they are carried out through the body. Baptism, then, is the circumcision of Christ, for it strips off the body of sin, which is the foreskin. As the foreskin is something superfluous to a Jew, so sin is to soul and body. He kept to this figure all the way through: by “the foreskin of the flesh” he means sin.

On Colossians 2:14–15: When the law that curses transgressors was given, all the people of Israel stood and shouted their assent to what was said and accepted it. Their assent became a kind of handwritten bond. Christ wiped out this bond, their assent to the law, by his own decrees. For he made rulings against the observances of the law. About foods, he ruled that it is not what goes into a man but what comes out of him that defiles him (Matthew 15:11). About keeping the Sabbath, he ruled by healing on the Sabbath. Anyone who looks will find many more of the same kind. So first of all, by his decrees he abolished the punishments the law laid on sinners for their sin, and he granted forgiveness of sins and repentance that leads to salvation. And because the people said “Amen” to the curses (Deuteronomy 27:15–26), the bond was set down as if signed. “Having stripped off the rulers and authorities, he made a public show of them, triumphing on the cross.” By stripping off and laying aside the flesh he brought down the opposing powers; so “having stripped off the rulers and authorities, he made a public show of them, triumphing over them in it.” Up to the cross and to death itself, it went unnoticed that our Lord was both God and Son of God. He astonished people with his miracles, but his body kept him veiled. That is why Satan tempted him: he wanted to find out whether he was the one the prophets had proclaimed, so that, if he learned that he was, he might block the saving plan. But the evil one got nowhere, because he could not find out; so for the time being Christ remained hidden. But once he had been nailed to the cross, had died, been buried and risen, and had fulfilled everything in the saving plan, he stripped off his hiddenness and showed openly, with his head uncovered, that the Godhead was there to be seen together with his body. The first work of God was the resurrection from the dead, then the ascent into heaven, and then the works done in his name through his servants and the other saints. So, having stripped off his hiddenness, he openly made a show of the opposing powers. And what was this show? That they have become weaker than …

choices.term: Τὴν ἐκκλησίαν λέγει πεπληρωμένην ὑπὸ τῆς θεότητος αὐτοῦ … ἥτις ἐστὶν ἡ ἐκκλησία;
choices.english: Doublet collapsed (Colossians 2:9–10): reduced to 'The second catena form adds:'
choices.why: Unmarked repetition of the note that opened at the end of u01-rem-mid ('he means the church, filled with the Godhead'; 'bodily = as a body to its head'). Added material kept: the Ephesians 1:23 quotation and the question 'why did he not add which is the church?'.

choices.term: ἐστὲ ἐν αὐτῷ πεπληρωμένοι, ἀντὶ τοῦ δι' αὐτοῦ πεπληρωμένοι
choices.english: “And you are filled in him” stands for “filled through him”.
choices.why: Lemma (2:10) and its explanation; the old English printed it as a lower-case fragment with no end.
rejected: you are filled in him, instead of being filled through him (old)

choices.term: ὡς περιττὸν δὲ ἀκροβυστία Ἰουδαίῳ, οὕτως ἁμαρτία ψυχῇ καὶ σώματι. διόλου δὲ τῇ τροπῇ παρέμεινεν.
choices.english: As the foreskin is something superfluous to a Jew, so sin is to soul and body. He kept to this figure all the way through
choices.why: τροπή = figure of speech (the circumcision figure); the old English 'Circumcision is for the Jew ... He remained in that way entirely' was garbled.
rejected: Circumcision is for the Jew, but sin is for soul and body. He remained in that way entirely.

choices.term: τοῦ νόμου τὰς τιμωρίας τὰς κατὰ τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν τοῖς δόγμασι τῆς ἁμαρτίας κατήργησεν
choices.english: by his decrees he abolished the punishments the law laid on sinners for their sin
choices.why: τῆς ἁμαρτίας taken with τὰς τιμωρίας ('punishments for sin'), τοῖς δόγμασι picking up Christ's decrees just mentioned. The old 'by the dogmas of sin' made Christ act by sin's decrees. The word order is odd and may be corrupt; noted in translator_notes.

choices.term: ἐλάνθανεν ὁ κύριος … τέως οὖν ἐλάνθανεν ὁ Χριστός
choices.english: it went unnoticed that our Lord was both God and Son of God … so for the time being Christ remained hidden
choices.why: λανθάνω = escape notice; the old English said the opposite ('was being revealed', 'finally Christ was revealed').
rejected: our Lord was being revealed as being both God and Son of God (old)

choices.why: Edition label; SOURCE_ISSUES item 4 noted the section was tagged 2:14-15 but opens on 2:10-11: each note now carries its own label (2:9–10 note continued, 2:11, 2:12–13, 2:14–15).

choices.term: ἐν ταῖς κατάραις ὁ λαὸς ἔλεγε τὸ ἀμήν
choices.english: the people said “Amen” to the curses (Deuteronomy 27:15–26)
choices.why: In Deuteronomy 27:15–26 'all the people shall say, Amen' after each curse.

choices.term: οὐ τὰ εἰσερχόμενα ἀλλὰ τὰ ἐξερχόμενα κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον
